Topic modeling is an unsupervised natural language processing method that infers latent themes from a collection of documents, representing each document as a mixture of topics and each topic as a weighted distribution over words. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is the most common algorithm; results depend on text preprocessing (tokenization, stop words, stemming), are judged with coherence measures and expert reading of top words, and can vary between runs because of random initialization.

## Ensemble LDA for a scoping review of TAM-targeting nanoparticles (2024)

Brown and coworkers applied Gensim's ensemble LDA, which clusters topics from many LDA runs with a DBSCAN variant to keep stable ones, to 854 screened abstracts on nanoparticles targeting tumor associated macrophages, after plain LDA gave noisy topics insensitive to hyperparameter tuning ([Brown et al. 2024](/papers/brown2024/)). Preprocessing used NLTK tokenization, English plus search-string-derived domain stop words, and Porter stemming. The model reached a C<sub>v</sub> coherence of 0.589 and gave six expert-interpretable topics (Immune and TAMs, Nanoparticles, Imaging, Biologics Delivery, Vaccines, Multi-modal Therapies), though only the two largest reappeared consistently across reruns. Applied without retraining to 95 newer abstracts it recovered five of the six topics, a proof of concept for a living review. Summary: [brown2024](/papers/brown2024/).
